bull_bear.body: Cash-rich balance sheet prioritizing organic growth; exploring asset-light models for new parks; no buyback or dividend specific guidance given, focus remains on funding future Tier-1 expansions once land deals conclude.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Land acquisition delays in Tier-1 cities; Weather variability (monsoons/heatwaves) impacting footfall; Regulatory hurdles (50-60 licenses required); Discretionary spend softness due to macro/geopolitical tensions; Water scarcity concerns (mitigated by own sources).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic on operational metrics but conservative on guidance due to macro uncertainty; transparent about land deal delays; confident in long-term 40% margin potential and Chennai's maturity curve.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly noted that repeat visitation is structurally low (2-3 year cycle) regardless of new rides, relying on fresh demographics (10-25 age group); Non-ticket revenue currently 30% but targeted to reach 50% in 4-5 years; Hyderabad underperformance partly due to a specific one-off ban on school groups (50k-60k loss).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Prudent Capital allocation: Disciplined capital allocation over the decades. Focus on generating substantial cash flows & maintaining debt free balance sheet."
- Consistent with the debt-free claim, the P&L shows a negligible finance cost - Rs 63.1 lakhs for FY26 - against total income of Rs 55,107.9 lakhs.
- Expansion (Bhubaneshwar, Chennai, The ISLE) has been executed alongside that debt-free stance, implying internal accrual funding, though the deck contains no cash flow statement or balance sheet to confirm it.
- The deck discloses no dividend, no buyback, no payout policy and no capital-raising plan.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Parks: Footfall 32.19 Lakh (+6% YoY); Q4 Footfall 8.79 Lakh (+30% YoY). Chennai contributed ~1.9 Lakh in Q4. Hyderabad footfall down 7% YoY due to weather/monsoon and school ban incidents. Resorts: Best-ever performance with improved occupancy; ISLE gaming pod driving incremental revenue.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "One of the Most visited parks in India: Wonderla parks have been visited by over 48 million* visitors since 2000, making us the most visited amusement park in India" (* as on 31st March 2026).
- "Two decades of experience (since launch of first park) in running parks in 5 different cities: Kochi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Bhubaneshwar and Chennai."
- Key strengths stated as: Superior Brand Recall ("Established as strong brand amongst visitors evidenced by better customer ratings & reviews"), in-house ride designing and manufacturing, strategic location, prudent capital allocation, and an experienced management team.
- Positioned as "A Complete Family Entertainment Destination" - "a rare avenue for families and friends to bond together in a wonderful outdoor environment" delivering "a safe, out-of-the-ordinary and highly memorable experience".
- Vision "Adding 'Wonder' to lives and bringing people closer"; mission to "Build and operate resource efficient amusement spaces to deliver a fun, thrilling, and hygienic experience to our guests".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Tax incentive] The Chennai park carries a Local Body Tax exemption for 10 years, granted in 2023 for the then-proposed park - a park-level cost advantage that runs well beyond the current year.
- [Corporate history] Veega Holidays was incorporated in 1998 to build the first park in Kochi (opened 2000 as "Veegaland"); Wonderla Holidays Limited was incorporated in 2002 for the Bengaluru park; Veega Holidays merged into Wonderla in 2008 and the Kochi park was renamed "Wonderla"; the company listed on both NSE and BSE in 2014.
- [Leadership] Executive Chairman & Managing Director Mr. Arun K. Chittilappilly, with Mr. Saji K Louiz as CFO and Mr. Dheeran Choudhary as COO; the board includes four independent directors.
- [Deck inconsistency] The "Strategic Location" strength refers to "All the three parks" while the company overview states five parks in five cities - an apparently un-updated slide rather than a change in footprint.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to 31% (vs historical 40%) due to Chennai launch costs, ESOP expenses, and Labor Code provisions. Depreciation expected to rise by INR 50-55 Cr in FY27 due to Chennai capitalization. Management expects margins to revert to 40% as Chennai scales and one-offs dissipate.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Optimistic for FY27 driven by full-year Chennai contribution. Margin: Targeting return to ~40% EBITDA historically achieved pre-expansion phase. Order Inflow: N/A. Capex: INR 35-40 Cr (sustaining) for FY27; no large greenfield capex planned until land deals close.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: N/A - Service business model; growth driven by footfall capacity and new park commissions rather than traditional order book.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Plan to add 5 new parks over next 5 years (2-3 likely to be announced/completed in this window); strategic shift from Tier-2 to Tier-1 cities (Mumbai, Delhi, Ahmedabad) causing land acquisition delays; Resort business expansion as adjacent high-margin vertical.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Wonderla delivered a record Q4 with 32% income growth driven by the new Chennai park, though FY26 PAT degrew 25% due to a high base of deferred tax benefits in the prior year. The core narrative shifts to margin normalization (targeting 40% EBITDA) as Chennai matures and management navigates significant delays in securing Tier-1 land for the next wave of expansion.

open.item: Margins at the newly commissioned Chennai park are expected to remain below those of mature parks in the initial stages, with gradual improvement as operations stabilise.
The Company is adopting a phased ramp-up approach for the Chennai park with a near-term focus on brand building and market development.
The Company continues to evaluate expansion opportunities across select locations, maintaining a pipeline of new park developments under evaluation backed by disciplined capital allocation.
The Company is focused on ARPU-led growth and monetisation driven by increasing contribution from non-ticket revenues including F&B, retail and hospitality.

QIP proceeds are earmarked for capital expenditure on the development of Wonderla Chennai Park, Glamping Pods and ancillary service areas at Wonderla Bengaluru, refurbishment at Wonderla Resort Bangalore, and setting up a roller coaster ride at Wonderla Park Bengaluru.

M/s. Deloitte Haskins & Sells are proposed for reappointment as Statutory Auditors for a second term of five consecutive years, from the conclusion of the 24th AGM until the conclusion of the 29th AGM, subject to Members' approval.
The Company intends to expand THE ISLE hospitality offering alongside the full-year operation and ramp-up of newer assets as its next phase of growth.

The Company will direct capital only toward expansion opportunities that meet tests of strategic fit, return potential and long-term value creation, growing in a measured and financially disciplined manner.
The Company evaluated renewable energy opportunities including rooftop solar installations and renewable power sourcing models, supported by solar-ready infrastructure at the Chennai park.

Given the scale of its water-based attractions, the Company will continue to enhance water utilisation efficiency through recycling, reuse and conservation, alongside waste segregation, composting and sustainable packaging across food service operations.
